en: Nasr ibn Ali al-Jahdhami narrated to us: Nuh ibn Qays informed us: Ibn Awn narrated to us, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah: that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to the delegation of Abd al-Qays: "I forbid you gourds, green earthen jars (hantam), hollowed stumps, and pitched vessels—and al-hantam is a large leather bag whose neck has been cut off—but drink from your water skin and tie it."

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Bahz narrated to us: Wuhayb narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): that he forbade pitched vessels, green earthen jars, and hollowed stumps. He said: It was said to Abu Hurayrah: "What is al-hantam?" He said: "Green jars."

He said: And Abu Salamah informed him that he heard Abu Hurayrah saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Do not prepare nabidh in gourds, nor in pitched vessels." Then Abu Hurayrah would say: "And avoid green earthen jars."

And Amr an-Naqid narrated to me: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from az-Zuhri, from Anas ibn Malik: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade that nabidh be prepared in gourds and pitched vessels.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik: that he informed him that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade that nabidh be prepared in gourds and pitched vessels.

And Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq narrated to me: Rawh narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us: Musa ibn Uqbah informed me, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, that he said: "It has been forbidden that unripe dates and fresh ripe dates be prepared together as nabidh, and that dried dates and raisins be prepared together."

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me: Abd ar-Razzaq narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: Musa ibn Uqbah informed me, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, that he used to say: "It has been forbidden that unripe dates and fresh ripe dates be prepared together as nabidh, and that dried dates and raisins be prepared together."

And Wahb ibn Baqiyyah narrated it to me: Khalid—meaning at-Tahhan—informed us, from ash-Shaybani, with this chain of narration, regarding dried dates and raisins, and he did not mention unripe dates and dried dates.

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from ash-Shaybani, from Habib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade that dried dates and raisins be mixed together, and that unripe dates and dried dates be mixed together; and he wrote to the people of Jurash forbidding them from mixing dried dates and raisins.

And Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated it to me: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us: Ikrimah ibn Ammar narrated to us: Yazid ibn Abd ar-Rahman ibn Udhaynah—and he is Abu Kathir al-Ghubari—narrated to us: Abu Hurayrah narrated to me, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said a similar narration.

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Abu Kurayb narrated to us—and the wording is Zuhayr's—they said: Waki' narrated to us, from Ikrimah ibn Ammar, from Abu Kathir al-Hanafi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade raisins with dried dates, and unripe dates with dried dates, and said: "Each one of them should be prepared as nabidh separately."
And Abu Salamah ibn Abd ar-Rahman narrated to me, from Abu Qatadah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), a hadith like this.

And Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq narrated to me: Affan ibn Muslim narrated to us: Aban al-Attar narrated to us: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us: Abdallah ibn Abi Qatadah narrated to me, from his father: that the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade the mixture of dried dates and unripe dates, the mixture of raisins and dried dates, and the mixture of partially ripened dates (zahw) and fresh ripe dates (rutab), and said: "Prepare each one separately as nabidh."

And Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq narrated it to me: Rawh ibn Ubadah narrated to us: Husayn al-Mu'allim narrated to us: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us, with these two chains of narration, except that he said: "fresh ripe dates and partially ripened dates, and dried dates and raisins."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us: Ali—and he is Ibn al-Mubarak—informed us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Qatadah: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Do not prepare partially ripened dates and fresh ripe dates together as nabidh, nor prepare fresh ripe dates and raisins together as nabidh; but rather prepare each one separately." And Yahya claimed that he met Abdallah ibn Abi Qatadah, who narrated to him from his father, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), a similar narration.
And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Bishr al-Abdi narrated to us, from Hajjaj ibn Abi Uthman, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, with this chain of narration, a similar narration.

Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to us: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us: Hisham ad-Dastawa'i informed us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abdallah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Do not prepare partially ripened dates and fresh ripe dates together as nabidh, nor prepare raisins and dried dates together as nabidh; rather, prepare each of them separately."

And Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq narrated it to me: Rawh ibn Ubadah narrated to us: Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Abdi narrated to us, with this chain of narration; he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade us to mix unripe dates with dried dates, or raisins with dried dates, or raisins with unripe dates; and he said: "Whoever among you drinks it..." and he mentioned a narration similar to the hadith of Waki'.

And Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Abdi, from Abu al-Mutawakkil an-Naji, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever among you drinks nabidh, let him drink it from raisins alone, or dried dates alone, or unripe dates alone."
And Nasr ibn Ali al-Jahdhami narrated to us: Bishr—meaning Ibn Mufaddal—narrated to us, from Abu Maslamah, with this chain of narration, a similar narration.

Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to us: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us: Sa'id ibn Yazid Abu Maslamah narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade us to mix raisins and dried dates, and to mix unripe dates and dried dates.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zuray' informed us, from at-Taymi, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id: that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade mixing dried dates and raisins, and mixing dried dates and unripe dates.

And Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us (H); and Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated to us: al-Layth informed us, from Abu az-Zubayr al-Makki, the freed slave of Hakim ibn Hizam, from Jabir ibn Abdillah al-Ansari, from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): that he forbade that raisins and dried dates be prepared together as nabidh, and forbade that unripe dates and fresh ripe dates be prepared together as nabidh.

And Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj (H); and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn Rafi's—they said: Abd ar-Razzaq narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us, who said: Ata' said to me: I heard Jabir ibn Abdillah saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Do not combine fresh ripe dates and unripe dates, nor raisins and dried dates, as nabidh."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us, from Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Jabir ibn Abdillah al-Ansari, from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): that he forbade that dried dates and raisins be prepared together as nabidh, and forbade that fresh ripe dates and unripe dates be prepared together as nabidh.

Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us: I heard Ata' ibn Abi Rabah; Jabir ibn Abdillah al-Ansari narrated to us: that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade mixing raisins and dried dates, and unripe dates and dried dates.

And Zuhayr ibn Harb and Abu Kurayb narrated to us—both saying: Waki' narrated to us, from al-Awza'i, Ikrimah ibn Ammar, and Uqbah ibn at-Taw'am, from Abu Kathir, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Khamr is from these two plants: the grapevine and the date-palm." And in the narration of Abu Kurayb: "the grapevines and the date-palms."

And Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: al-Awza'i narrated to us: Abu Kathir narrated to us, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "Khamr is from these two plants: the date-palm and the grapevine."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: al-Hajjaj ibn Abi Uthman informed us: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to me that Abu Kathir narrated to him, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Khamr is from these two trees: the date-palm and the grapevine."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Alqamah ibn Wa'il, from his father, Wa'il al-Hadrami: that Tariq ibn Suwayd al-Ju'fi asked the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) about wine, and he forbade him or disliked that he should make it. Tariq said: "I only make it for medicine." So he said: "Indeed, it is not a medicine; rather, it is a disease."
